### Universal health coverage (CMU)

The CMU aims to guarantee access to quality healthcare for the entire population residing in Ivory Coast, through two schemes:

A contributory scheme, called the General Basic Scheme (RGB), at a rate of 1,000 CFA francs per person per month;
and a non-contributory scheme, called the Medical Assistance Scheme (RAM), which targets low-income individuals, in which the state acts as the insured's substitute for the payment of contributions and co-payments.
The management of these two schemes has been entrusted to the Social Welfare Institution, called the National Health Insurance Fund (IPS-CNAM), created by decree no. 2014-395 of June 25, 2014.
The CNAM launched its operations on December 30, 2014, with the enrollment of His Excellency Mr. The benefits for both the government and its citizens are numerous and diverse: in particular, the digitization of exchanges reduces management and travel costs, supports economic development, enhances transparency, and improves the quality of services provided.

In line with this focus on efficiency, the Ivorian government has launched its new public portal for administrative procedures. This portal aims to centralize all administrative procedures, whether already digitized or not. Through a modern and user-friendly graphical interface accessible from a computer, tablet, or smartphone, the portal has a dual objective:
For digitized procedures, the site provides access to all the information necessary to complete the process and offers a direct link to the online application.

For procedures currently being digitized, the portal offers all the information necessary for the user to prepare their documentation and facilitate their request when they visit an Administration counter.

The development of this portal is a dynamic and ongoing process. Therefore, aware of the work that remains to be done, the Administration provides a suggestion module that allows you to quickly propose improvements so that the portal better meets your needs.
